questions.prompt: Why is a loop in a switched LAN so harmful?
options: Broadcasts circulate forever, since Ethernet frames have no time-to-live, causing a broadcast storm

questions.prompt: What does STP stand for? (three words)
STP removes redundant links by making you unplug them.
Which switch becomes the root bridge?
options: The one with the lowest bridge ID (priority, then MAC address)
The one with the most ports
The one with the highest MAC address

questions.prompt: What's the default STP bridge priority? (a number)
SW1 has priority 32768 and MAC AAA. SW2 has priority 4096 and MAC BBB. Which is root?
options: SW1, because its MAC is lower
SW2, because its priority is lower

questions.prompt: What's the name for a switch's port on its cheapest path to the root bridge? (two words)
What does a port in the learning state do?
options: Adds MAC addresses to the table, but doesn't forward frames yet

questions.prompt: Put the STP port states in order, from a port just coming up to fully active.
RSTP was created because classic STP can take 30 to 50 seconds to bring a port to forwarding.
What are the messages switches exchange to run STP called? (five letters)
